Treatment summary
Patient presented following a side-impact collision at an intersection with complaints of neck and back pain. The
mechanism of injury is consistent with the reported strain, and the force of the impact is in keeping with the soft tissue
injuries described. Over the course of 22 visits, care included manual therapy, targeted exercise, and home program
instruction. Treatment followed a typical progression and was gradually reduced as symptoms improved. On
examination, some findings, including reduced cervical ragne of motion and paraspinal muscle tenderness, support
the reported injury, while other neurological and orthopedic tests were within nromal limits. Prior records document
ongoing care for similar neck and back complaints before this collision, and much of the current symptom burden
appears to reflect that pre-existing condition rahter than the recent event. Billing reviewed for this episode shows no
duplicate or repeated charges. Ongoing recommendations include continued home exercise and reassessment if
symptoms change.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
